content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese is a fresh cheese curd product obtained by curdling milk and draining the whey. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor and a creamy, slightly grainy texture. Cottage cheese is eaten on its own, used in cooking, baking, desserts, and as a high-protein snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese has been a staple in many cultures for centuries, appearing in traditional dishes worldwide.
Its fat content varies widely, from non‑fat varieties to those containing up to 9‑10 % milk fat.
It is commonly used as a base for cheese spreads, dips, and creamy desserts.
In the United States, cottage cheese is often served with fruit, honey, or as a topping for salads.
The curds can be small and fine or larger and more distinct, depending on the processing method.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides a complete source of protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium in cottage cheese contributes to strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in fat (in low‑fat versions)
items.content: Reduced‑fat cottage cheese delivers nutrients with fewer calories.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Live cultures present in some cottage cheese varieties may promote gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience digestive discomfort after consuming cottage cheese.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some flavored or salted cottage cheeses can be high in sodium; choose low‑salt options if you watch your salt intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein, the main protein in cottage cheese, should avoid it.

items.title: Shelf‑life considerations
items.content: Cottage cheese spoils quickly; keep it refrigerated and consume within the indicated date after opening.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be enjoyed on its own, mixed into smoothies, used to make cheese pancakes, baked dishes, as a filling for crepes and dumplings, or combined with fruit, berries, or honey for a sweet snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C to 4 °C. It can be frozen for longer storage, though the texture may become crumbly after thawing.
